Sometimes the best aviation gathering is at a small airport with its doors wide open. ✈️💛

Rio Vista Municipal Airport in Northern California celebrated its fifth Airport Day on September 12. In an October 8 firsthand report, General Aviation News contributor Hayman Tam describes a free community event filled with kitplanes, warbirds and flying displays.

SeaRey amphibians, Glasairs, Rutan designs and Van’s homebuilts shared the ramp. Beech T-34 Mentors and a Nanchang CJ-6 added a dose of aviation history, while RV pilots and the volunteer Memorial Squadron demonstrated formation flying.

Collector cars, food vendors and a STEM display rounded out the day.

It’s a reminder of what local airports can offer: a place to meet builders, discover unfamiliar aircraft and see general aviation up close.

Here’s to the pilots, volunteers and airport teams who welcome their communities onto the ramp. 🛩️
